conviction_note: The quarter looks set to beat: the company guided Q3 to about 17% of a FY guide of at least $27 (about $4.59), consensus is $4.66-4.84, and on 2026-09-10 management said Q3 was tracking ahead. UNH's 2026-10-13 MCR beat is a positive read-across. But ELV has sold its last three beats (-8.5% on Q2 2026's beat-and-raise, -12.2% in Q2 2025, -1.2% on a 21% Q3 2025 beat), the stock is at its 52-week high after +9% in 20 days, and 2027 consensus (~$29.3) sits right on the company's floor of 12% growth off at least $26. So the findings sum to +0.3, p_up is 52, and the scaled number is +0.26 on a 6.5% absolute move. The fundamental read (+6% EPS beat) and the reaction read (near zero) diverge on purpose: this name trades on margins and the forward guide, not on the beat.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS. Company guide: CFO on the 2026-07-15 call said Q3 would be about 17% of FY guidance of at least $27.00, i.e. about $4.59 (https://s202.q4cdn.com/665319960/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/ELV-USQ_Transcript_2026-07-15.pdf, p.6). FY guide reaffirmed in an 8-K on 2026-09-10: adjusted EPS at least $27.00, benefit expense ratio 90.2% +/- 50bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1156039/000115603926000063/elv-20260910.htm). Street: Zacks $4.66 on $48.6B revenue, Benzinga ~$4.70 on $49.0B, Earnings Whispers $4.84 (search snippets, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ELV/earnings-forecasts, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ELV). I sized against ~$4.70, which two estimate sources agree on and which sits just above the company's implied figure. 2027 bar: the company floor is at least 12% growth off at least $26 = at least $29.12; consensus is ~$29.25-29.44 (Barchart/Yahoo, TIKR, dated mid-2026, so possibly stale).
positioning_check: FINRA short interest at settlement 2026-09-30: 4.85M shares, 3.92 days to cover, ~2.24% of shares outstanding. That is down from 6.03M at 2026-07-15, and the 2026-10-15 figure is not yet published (https://equibles.com/stocks/elv/shortinterest, read 2026-10-20). Not a crowded short. The baseline skew is +2.82 vol points (25d put IV minus call IV), mildly downside-paid, with put/call OI at 1.05. ATM IV is 39.9% against 19.7% 20-day realised, so the options price a large event (7.61% event-implied move). The stock is at its 52-week high (+9.09% over 20d, +3.23% over 5d).

findings.finding: Q3 is guided at about $4.59 and the company said it is running ahead. On the 2026-07-15 call the CFO said Q3 adjusted EPS would be about 17% of FY guidance of at least $27 (about $4.59), and that the $0.80 Q2 below-the-line gain would fund one-time H2 investments. At the 2026-09-10 Wells Fargo conference management reportedly said Q3 adjusted EPS was 'tracking ahead of prior expectations due to favorable benefit expense performance', with MA ahead, Medicaid slightly ahead of the -1.75% margin outlook and individual ACA modestly better. The same day's 8-K only reaffirmed FY at least $27 and the 90.2% +/-50bp benefit expense ratio. Consensus of $4.66-4.84 already sits above the company's implied $4.59.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has not paid for EPS beats. Q2 2026 beat ($7.45 vs ~$6.20) with a raise to at least $27 and fell -8.54%. Q3 2025 beat ($6.03 vs $4.98 Zacks) and moved -1.22%. Q2 2025 fell -12.22%. Q1 2026 was +0.03%. Only Q4 2025 (+5.86%) paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The tracking comment has been public for six weeks and the stock is +9% over 20 days. If it were fully in the estimates, consensus would sit well above the $4.66 Zacks figure, which instead carries one downward revision and no upward ones in 60 days. The upside left is the size of the beat. Caveat: the 'tracking ahead' wording comes from a third-party AI summary, and the primary 8-K says only 'reaffirm'.
findings.independence: The 17% seasonality figure is from the primary transcript (https://s202.q4cdn.com/665319960/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/ELV-USQ_Transcript_2026-07-15.pdf), and the reaffirmation from the primary 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1156039/000115603926000063/elv-20260910.htm). Both are company documents, so this is one source family.

findings.finding: UnitedHealth reported on 2026-10-13, after ELV last spoke. Its Q3 2026 medical care ratio was 88.4% against ~89.9% expected (89.9% a year ago), adjusted EPS was $4.69 against ~$4.12, and FY adjusted EPS guidance went to at least $20.50 from $19.50-20.00. Reportedly it also lifted its 2026 core Medicaid margin to 'moderately better than -1%'. The quality is lower than the headline: $610M of the improvement was favorable 2026 reserve development, and Medicaid membership fell 10.3% year on year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the UNH print day ELV rose about 2% to $429.47 against +0.7% for XLV (247wallst, 2026-10-13). It is now $439. ELV's own reactions after favorable peer prints are not in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: ELV moved +2% that day and has kept rising. What may not be in ELV's Q3 consensus is the read-across to its government books. Zacks still shows a downward revision, which suggests estimates were not raised after UNH. If the read-across were fully priced, ELV's Q3 estimates would have moved up after 10-13.
findings.independence: UNH beat vs consensus and the guide raise: https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/news-and-research/unitedhealth-group-shares-gain-3-after-stronger-than-expected-earnings-and-guidance. Medicaid trough and reserve share: https://finsee.ai/earnings/unh/2026/q3/en/. Both read the same UNH release.

findings.finding: The 2027 bar sits on the company's own floor. Management has committed to at least 12% adjusted EPS growth in 2027 off a baseline of at least $26 (CFO, 2026-07-15 call; reaffirmed 2026-09-10), which is at least $29.12. Consensus 2027 is about $29.25-29.44 (Barchart, TIKR, mid-2026). A Q3 call that simply restates 'at least 12%' therefore lands in line. Risks to the 2027 framing that the call may address: Medicaid exits and attrition (750k members expected lost in 2026), the ACA risk pool after subsidies expired, and the fall in 4-star-plus members for 2028 payments.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a raise to at least $27 alongside heavier reinvestment was sold 8.5%. Q4 2025 (first 2026 guide, framed 'prudent'): +5.86%. Guide moves drive this name's largest reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock at its 52-week high and options at 39.9% IV both say the market expects a confirming or better 2027 message. If a cautious framing were priced, the stock would not be at highs with only a mild +2.8 skew. Whether the company goes beyond 'at least 12%' is not knowable from public sources.
findings.independence: 2027 consensus: https://finance.yahoo.com/sectors/healthcare/articles/elevance-health-earnings-preview-expect-095802575.html (Barchart, $29.25) and https://www.tikr.com/blog/elevance-health-reaffirms-25-5-eps-guidance-amid-cms-pressure-380-mean-target-intact ($29.44). UNH said on 10-13 that 2027 consensus 'may understate' its own opportunity (search snippet), a mild offset.

findings.finding: Elevance's 2027 MA star ratings, released by CMS on 2026-10-08, slipped. Per Stephens, 45% of its members are in 4-star-plus plans, down from 53%. Becker's puts the unweighted average at 3.51, down from 3.59. Capstone called the result 'slightly positive' against expectations. Elevance is also suing CMS over a $115M 2026 ratings differential. The stars set 2028 bonus payments, so the effect is on the outlook beyond 2027, not on Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history on stars. The stock kept rising after 10-08.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it has been public for 12 days and the stock rose since. The only unpriced part is whether management quantifies a 2028 headwind on the call. Snippet only (403 on fetch).
findings.independence: Same data via https://www.beckerspayer.com/?p=29667 (snippet, 403) and the lawsuit via https://www.healthcarefinancenews.com/news/elevance-sues-cms-over-115m-medicare-advantage-star-ratings-dispute.

findings.finding: Peer read on commercial cost trend. UnitedHealthcare said in July 2026 that commercial medical cost trend was running 'modestly above 11%' and rising, with No Surprises Act arbitration adding at least 100bp. That is a proxy for ELV's large commercial risk book. ELV itself said on 2026-09-10 that employer cost trend is 'elevated but consistent with pricing assumptions'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Commercial has not been the line ELV's reactions turned on recently; Medicaid and government margins were (Q2 2026, Q2 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy, published before ELV's own September statement. If commercial overruns were priced, ELV would not be at a 52-week high. The finding is small because the company-level statement points the other way.
findings.independence: Proxy only. ELV's own counter-statement is in the Wells Fargo summary: https://quartr.com/events/elevance-health-inc-elv-wells-fargo-21st-annual-healthcare-conference_3e3sMhyM

findings.finding: ACA risk-pool proxy. CMS February 2026 effectuated marketplace enrollment fell about 13% (22.1M to 19.2M) after enhanced subsidies expired. Molina cut its 2026 Marketplace outlook to a $0.75/share loss in July. ELV said in July it would end 2026 with at least 1M individual members and was re-establishing much of the 2025 risk-adjustment favorability in its 2026 accrual. On 2026-09-10 it said ACA was modestly better than expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Individual ACA was a positive contributor in ELV's Q2 2026, which still sold off on other lines.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry proxy, well known. ELV's own disclosures say its book is doing better and that it is carrying a cushion (prudent risk-adjustment accrual), which caps the downside, so this is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Molina Q2 2026 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001179929/000117992926000036/moh2q26_er.htm. ELV counter-evidence is in its Q2 transcript (same document as finding 1).

baseline_tension: My lean is mildly positive. That runs slightly against the +2.82 put skew and rides a +9% 20-day run-up to a 52-week high, which is the setup in which this name has sold good quarters, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction) plus lesson 6 (the beat lands inside what the company told the market to expect on 09-10): Q3 tracking-ahead finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5, because ELV sold its last three beats.

Lesson 5 (a company-level statement beats a proxy): the commercial cost-trend proxy went from -0.3 to -0.15 and the ACA proxy from -0.1 to -0.05, because ELV's own September statements point the other way.
Lesson 7 (positioning): a mildly positive sign against +2.82 skew with a non-crowded short (3.9 DTC), so p_up moved from 53 to 52.
Core/lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move raised from 6.0 to 6.5 because the Q3 call is likely to carry 2027 framing, which is guidance-scale for this name.
Left standing: the UNH peer-print finding (+0.5; 'a peer's print landing after the company last spoke' is on the list of what has paid), the 2027 bar finding (-0.3) and the stars finding (-0.2).
